criterion: Running prose across the run board and the balance screen is set in a serif face at a measure of roughly seventy characters.
evaluation_rule: A measure is the width of a line of text. Yes if body copy, headings and table cells on the console surfaces are set in a serif family and a line of body copy runs to around seventy characters before wrapping. No if a sans-serif family carries the running prose, or if a line of body copy runs the full width of a wide window.

criterion: Every state that carries consequence on the run board, the balance screen and the certificate register is written as a word beside any colour used for the same state.
evaluation_rule: The states that carry consequence are a non-claimable batch, a lapsed calibration, an open deviation, an unreviewed override, a withdrawn certificate, a planned capacity row, a claim type on a compact figure and an unreachable contract floor. Yes if each of those reads as a word wherever it appears and green is absent from every console surface. No if any of them is signalled by a colour or an icon alone, or if a figure is tinted green so as to read as a verdict.

criterion: The balance screen prints its remaining margin as a mass in grams.
evaluation_rule: The margin is the claimable mass still available in the period. Yes if the balance screen prints a figure in grams for the margin and prints the override, restatement and finding counts as bare numerals at the same visual emphasis as the rest of the table. No if the margin reads as a status phrase such as within limits, or if a count sits inside a coloured pill.

criterion: A refused allocation on the balance screen raises an inline banner carrying the available mass beside the requested mass.
evaluation_rule: An inline banner sits in the flow of the surface that produced the act, rather than floating over it and disappearing. Yes if the banner names what was refused, prints both masses, says what would change the outcome, and every figure already on the screen stays as it was. No if the refusal appears as a floating toast, or if the banner carries only a generic failure message.

criterion: An empty console collection says so in a sentence, and a surface awaiting data says the surface is loading.
evaluation_rule: Yes if an empty batch register, an empty certificate register and an empty restatement list each render a sentence naming what is absent, and a surface still fetching prints a loading line. No if an empty collection renders as a blank frame or as a bare table head, or if a loading surface renders as an empty one.

criterion: An unsatisfied issuing condition on the certificate wizard names the record that would resolve the block and links to that record.
evaluation_rule: The eight issuing conditions are shown as eight statements on every step of the wizard. Yes if an unsatisfied statement names the blocking record, such as an unreviewed override on a lot, and offers a link to it, and every control on the screen leaves the block standing. No if the statement reads as a generic failure, or if any control on the screen sets the condition aside.

criterion: The withdrawal screen prints the recipients by name and the statements that become void before the person confirms.
evaluation_rule: Yes if the screen lists each recipient who will be notified as a named row and lists each downstream statement the recipient must stop making, both before the confirming control. No if the screen prints a count of recipients instead of the list, or if the lists appear only after confirmation.

criterion: Signing a certificate is a separate act on the review step that states the recipient will file the document with a regulator.
evaluation_rule: Yes if the review step renders the document, carries one control whose label names signing rather than saving, and prints a sentence saying the recipient files the document with a regulator. No if signing shares a control with moving between steps, or if the consequence sentence is absent from the review step.

criterion: The console carries one persistent top bar whose controls match the role the reader holds.
evaluation_rule: Yes if the same top bar appears on every console surface and an auditor session shows reading and export controls alone. No if navigation moves into a side rail on some surfaces, or if a mutating control renders for a reader whose role forbids the act.

criterion: Labels take the grotesk, identifiers and column figures take the monospace, and hierarchy comes from size with one heavier stroke on the two largest steps.
evaluation_rule: Yes if field labels, table headers and the top bar are set in a sans face, lot references and masses in tables are set in a fixed-width face whose figures align down a column, and only the two largest heading steps carry a heavier stroke. No if masses in a column fail to line up, or if three or more stroke levels appear across the console.

criterion: The public routes show photographed pellets and waste imagery that reads as mixed contaminated material.
evaluation_rule: Yes if the pellet imagery reads as a photograph of real granulate rather than a render, and the waste imagery shows mixed, coloured, contaminated textile rather than clean sorted offcuts. No if the pellets read as a synthetic render, or if the waste imagery shows tidy single-colour material.

criterion: Motion across the product reads as eased, with entrances and exits settling once and each transition declared against a named property.
evaluation_rule: An eased transition accelerates and decelerates on a curve rather than overshooting its endpoint. Yes if panels, banners and menus settle in one movement and each transition names the property it animates. No if any element overshoots and springs back, or if a transition is declared across every property at once.

criterion: Headings on the public routes come into focus from a blur as the reader reaches them, resolving through one shared distance and duration.
evaluation_rule: Yes if a heading below the fold begins blurred and transparent, sharpens as the reader arrives, is legible before the movement ends, and every heading on every public route uses the same distance and duration. No if headings only fade in, or if a figure counts up as it changes.

criterion: Text across the product meets WCAG AA contrast at every size, sits at twelve pixels or above, and every icon-only control carries a label.
evaluation_rule: Yes if body copy, labels and disabled text all clear the AA ratio against their ground, the smallest rendered text measures twelve pixels or more, focus rings are visible on every focusable element, and each icon-only control carries a text label or an accessible name. No if any text falls below twelve pixels, or if an icon-only control reaches a reader as an unnamed glyph.

criterion: The focus treatment differs from the hover treatment, and keyboard navigation reaches every control a pointer reaches.
evaluation_rule: Yes if tabbing to a control produces a visibly different treatment from hovering the same control, and every menu, dialog and wizard step is reachable and operable from the keyboard alone. No if focus and hover render alike, or if any control is reachable only under a pointer.

criterion: The genealogy graph, the balance screen and the certificate wizard each reflow into a single column at a phone width.
evaluation_rule: Yes if the graph becomes the nested list, the balance table becomes one figure per row, and the wizard becomes one condition per row, each carrying the same facts as the wide arrangement. No if any of the three shrinks its wide arrangement into an unreadable version of itself.

criterion: Every route holds its layout from a narrow phone to a wide desktop under one breakpoint system.
evaluation_rule: Yes if each public and console route renders usably at a phone, a tablet and a desktop width, the breakpoints repeat the same widths across the whole product, the document itself stays free of sideways scrolling, and a wide table scrolls inside its own container. No if a route forces the document to scroll sideways, or if two different sets of breakpoint widths appear.

criterion: The reconciliation view leads on the mass balance residual, and the replay result gives agreement the same visual emphasis as disagreement.
evaluation_rule: The residual is the mass the period cannot account for, and a reader expects the figure to be other than zero. Yes if the residual is the first and largest figure on the reconciliation view, and the replay result renders a matching figure and a differing figure in the same size, colour and weighting. No if the residual is buried among the other five figures, or if a disagreement is styled as an alarm and an agreement as a reassurance.

criterion: The palette across the public routes reads warm rather than neutral, with the quiet text a clear step lighter than the reading text.
evaluation_rule: The brief names six roles by the job each does and states no colour value, so the build picks all six. Yes if the page ground is a warm off-white rather than a grey or a pure white, and a secondary label reads as quieter than body copy at a glance while still being legible. No if the ground is neutral grey or pure white, or if a secondary label is either indistinguishable from body copy or too faint to read.
